([[Wynnewood, Pennsylvania]]) | college = [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] (2017–2019) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2019]]) *Second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] ([[2019 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2019]]) *Third-team All-American – [[Associated Press|AP]], [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]], [[Sporting News|SN]] (2019) *[[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]] (2019) *First-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] (2019) *ACC Defensive Player of the Year (2019) *ACC Sixth Man of the Year (2018) *ACC All-Freshman Team (2018) }} '''De'Andre James Hunter''' (born December 1, 1997) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]]. ==High school career== Hunter attended [[Friends' Central School]] in [[Wynnewood, Pennsylvania]]. As a junior, he averaged 21.6 points, 11.0 rebounds, and 5.0 assists per game, while being named Pennsylvania Class AA Player of the Year. As a senior in 2016, Hunter averaged 23.5 points, 9.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.5 blocks per game. Hunter was rated as a four-star recruit and ranked as the 72nd overall recruit and 14th best small forward in the 2016 high school class.{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/186502/deandre-hunter|title=DeAndre Hunter - basketball recruiting - player profiles|last=|first=|date=|work=www.espn.com|access-date=April 25, 2016}} On September 12, 2015, Hunter committed to [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], choosing UVA over other offers from [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] & [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]].{{Cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2565773-deandre-hunter-to-virginia-cavaliers-land-4-star-sg-prospect|title=DeAndre Hunter to Virginia: Cavaliers land 4-star SG Prospect|last=|first=|date=|work=www.bleacherreport.com|access-date=September 12, 2015}} ==College career== During his redshirt freshman season, Hunter scored double figures in 16 games, including in 11 conference games. During a game against [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], Hunter scored the final 3 pointer to win the game at the buzzer.{{cite web|title=Watch: No. 1 Virginia Beats Louisville Despite Being Down 4 With a Second Left|author=Carroll, Charlotte|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/01/virginia-Louisville-buzzer-beater-crazy-ending|date=March 1, 2018|accessdate=July 2, 2018|work=Sports Illustrated}} Hunter broke his wrist during the [[2018 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|2018 ACC tournament]] and could not play in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2018 NCAA tournament]].{{cite web|title=Virginia's De'Andre Hunter Will Miss NCAA Tournament Due to Broken Wrist|author=Rollins, Khadrice|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/13/virginia-deandre-hunter-miss-ncaa-tournament-broken-wrist|date=March 13, 2018|accessdate=July 2, 2018|work=Sports Illustrated}} Without Hunter, the number 1 seed Virginia went on to lose in the first round to the number 16 seed, [[UMBC Retrievers men's basketball|UMBC]]. After this season, Hunter was named to the All-ACC All-Freshman team, as well as being named the ACC Sixth man of the year.{{cite web|title=ACC ANNOUNCES ALL-CONFERENCE TEAM, POSTSEASON AWARDS|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/2018/3/4/mens-basketball-acc-announces-all-conference-team-postseason-awards.aspx|date=March 4, 2018|accessdate=July 2, 2018|website=theacc.com}} In his freshman season, Hunter posted 9.2 points and 3.5 rebounds per game. Hunter later announced that he would return to Virginia for the 2018-2019 season despite speculation that he could declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=De'Andre Hunter, who might have been a first-round pick in this year's NBA Draft, is returning to Virginia|author=Norlander, Matt|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/deandre-hunter-who-might-have-been-a-first-round-pick-in-this-years-nba-draft-is-returning-to-virginia/|date=April 20, 2018|accessdate=July 2, 2018|work=CBS Sports}} In his sophomore season, Hunter averaged 15.2 points per game and 5.1 rebounds per game. He helped lead Virginia to another #1 seed in the [[2019_NCAA_Division_I_Men%27s_Basketball_Tournament|2019 NCAA Tournament]]. Virginia would win the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|2019 Championship game]] 85-77 behind Hunter's 27 points and 9 rebounds. Following his second season, Hunter announced his intention to forgo his final two seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]], where he is projected to be a first round selection.{{Cite news|url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/virginia-guard-de-andre-hunter-declares-for-nba-draft/article_dff48e18-5fb7-11e9-884d-1ff517e74fed.html|title=Virginia guard
